documents.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) form the basis of multiple generative applications today, but these systems are mostly stateless which means that information keeps outside the context window disappears when the session is closed. Such limitations complicate personalization, make it difficult to maintain consistency over long interactions, and prevent the AI system from learning from its experience. Lifelong memory architectures address this problem by providing the LLM with an external, permanent memory that also includes means of information writing, retrieval, updating, consolidating, and forgetting without the need to retrain the model itself. This paper presents an overview of the developments in this area starting from early external-memory enhancement and reflective generative agents, and continuing with memory operating system, graph-shaped memory, and reinforcement learning of agent memory. We summarize our results, suggesting an operation-centered classification of such systems and compare such twelve representations with regard to scalability, retrieval efficiency, personalization, computational cost, and adaptability, discussing necessary technologies such as embeddings, approximate nearest neighbor index, knowledge graph, and retrieval-augmented generation.

Abstract The relationship between literature and technology has always been dynamic. From the invention of the printing press to the emergence of digital books, social media, artificial intelligence, virtual reality, and other digital platforms, technological developments have continuously influenced the ways in which literature is produced, distributed, read, and interpreted. In the contemporary period, emerging technologies have created new possibilities for literary expression while also raising important questions about authorship, creativity, originality, reading practices, and the future of the literary text. Artificial Intelligence (AI), digital humanities, electronic literature, virtual reality, augmented reality, and online publishing are particularly significant in this transformation. This paper examines the changing relationship between literature and emerging technologies. The paper contends that we should not view technology solely as a tool for reproducing traditional literature. Rather, it has become an active force that changes the form, structure, circulation, and interpretation of literary works. Digital platforms have made literature more accessible and interactive, while artificial intelligence has introduced new possibilities for writing, translation, editing, and literary analysis. At the same time, these developments have generated concerns regarding plagiarism, copyright, authorship, misinformation, algorithmic bias, and the possible loss of human creativity. The paper therefore considers both the opportunities and challenges created by emerging technologies in literary studies. It concludes that literature is unlikely to disappear in the technological age; instead, it is evolving into new forms that require readers and scholars to rethink the meaning of authorship, text, reading, and creativity.

Abstract Literature and technology have had a dynamic relationship throughout. Technology has always affected the creation, dissemination, reading and interpretation of the written word – from the invention of the printing press through digital books, social media, artificial intelligence, and virtual reality. The new technologies that have developed in the modern era have opened up new avenues for the expression of literature, as well as raised new issues of authorship, creativity, originality, reading practices, and the future of the literary text. Of course, Digital Humanities, electronic literature, virtual reality, augmented reality and online publishing are especially important in this shift.In this paper I'm exploring the evolving relationship between literature and new technologies. The paper argues against the notion that technology is just a means to copy traditional literature. Instead, it has become an active entity which alters the form, structure, circulation and interpretation of literary works. New possibilities for writing, translation, editing and literary analysis have been opened by the use of AI, and digital platforms have made literature more accessible and interactive. Meanwhile, such changes have raised concerns about plagiarism, copyright, authorship, misinformation, algorithmic bias and the potential for a loss of human creativity. So the paper discusses the opportunities and challenges of the new technologies in the study of literature. It argues that in the technological era literature will not be abolished, but is mutating into new forms that force readers and scholars to reconsider what it means to be an author, a text, a reader, and a creator. The fields of literature and emerging technologies merge in the Electronic Literature collection. The collection of Electronic Literature brings together the fields of literature and emerging technologies.

The increasing complexity of ethical dilemmas in higher education, particularly those involving digital technology, has increased scholarly interest in college students’ moral reasoning. However, previous reviews have focused mainly on theoretical perspectives or ethics education interventions, with limited attention to the intellectual structure of this research field. This study maps the intellectual and thematic organization of research on college students’ moral reasoning and examines the emergence of digital ethics and artificial intelligence within the literature. A total of 677 documents published between 1983 and 2024 in the Web of Science Core Collection were analyzed using VOSviewer for co-citation and keyword analyses, following a PRISMA-based screening procedure. The findings show that Kohlberg’s theory of moral development and Rest’s Four-Component Model form major foundations of the field, while recent thematic developments include digital ethics, academic integrity, artificial intelligence, virtual simulations, and cross-cultural moral education. The study provides a systematic bibliometric knowledge map and identifies emerging and underexplored areas for future theoretical and empirical research.

Abstract Marketing management is no longer about selling and promoting goods, but it is about creating, communicating, delivering and sustaining the value to the customers. Marketing managers have access to a range of new tools which have grown significantly due to digital platforms, social media, e-commerce, data analytics, marketing automation and AI. Meanwhile, there is ever more demand for relevance, convenience, transparency, personalisation, responsible data use and meaningful brand experiences. This is a conceptual research paper that addresses the nature of marketing management in the digital age and creates an integration of market orientation, segmentation and positioning, customer experience, digital communication, data-driven decision making, artificial intelligence, brand management, relationship marketing and sustainability. The psaper has been drawn from literature review of the existing marketing-management literature, digital-marketing literature and selected Marathi reference sources. The study is based on conceptual synthesis and managerial implications because there is no primary survey or fabricated numerical data. The review shows that the effective marketing management in the contemporary world needs a balance between technology and judgment of human beings. While Data and AI can enhance targeting, prediction, personalization and measurement, customer trust, ethical communication, privacy, brand purpose and human centred service are still vital. The paper suggests a practical sequence of actions: getting to know the market, customer value definition, identification of priority segments, the creation of an integrated value proposition, the activation of digital and physical touch points, measuring results, constant learning and embedding of responsible marketing. The framework is especially relevant for organizations that are in competitive, digital and rapidly changing markets.

Benchmark package for the study "Can large language models read cell-free RNA expression panels for fibrosis staging in MASLD?" Twelve frontier LLMs were scored against classical machine-learning gates (logistic regression, HistGradientBoosting) on three task families — binary advanced fibrosis, 5-class staging, and ordinal 0–4 — using text-formatted cfRNA prompts derived from the top-200 MAD genes of the Ghent plasma cell-free transcriptome cohort (Poma-Soto et al.). This version contains the Colab notebooks (prompt construction, baseline and frontier evaluation, automated run drivers, C3 evaluations, v6 fine-tune and evaluation), the static benchmark site (task catalogue, methods, models, leaderboards with bootstrap confidence intervals), one summary figure, and a frontier-model run log. It does NOT contain per-sample gene-expression values or the full prompt texts, which derive from EGA-gated data (EGAD50000000775, Ghent DAC Data Usage Agreement). The archived analysis plans, run/deviation log, and corpus manifest are not included in this version.Acknowledgements The Ghent cohort was generated by the Ghent University research groups responsible for the plasma cell-free RNA biobank and cohort, who act as the Ghent DAC for the EGA deposition (EGAD50000000775 / EGAS50000000545). Subhadip Banerjee acknowledges the Research Foundation – Flanders (FWO), which allocated a grant for a scientific stay in Flanders (file ID V504225N, hosted at the University of Antwerp). Rawiwan Charoensub acknowledges the Ursimone Wietlisbach Foundation for grant support.

The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) provides opportunities to support the learning process, but it also presents challenges related to ethics, data security, academic integrity, and responsible use of digital technology. This community service activity aimed to improve AI literacy among students and parents by strengthening their understanding of safe, ethical, and responsible AI use. The activity was conducted at SDN 25 Madello over a two-month period, involving students and parents as participants. The method employed an educational-participatory approach through material delivery, discussions, practical activities, case studies, and evaluation. The materials covered an introduction to AI, the use of AI in learning, AI ethics, academic integrity, personal data protection and security, and legal awareness in the digital environment. The activity was conducted through collaboration among the fields of Education, Constitutional Law, and Islamic Family Law. The results indicated an improvement in participants’ understanding of the benefits and risks of AI use, as well as the importance of verifying information, protecting personal data, and using AI responsibly. The activity also demonstrated the importance of parental involvement in supporting children’s AI use at home. Cross-disciplinary collaboration provided a comprehensive approach to developing a generation that is aware, critical, and responsible in utilizing AI.

documents.abstract: Background: Nurses serve as the primary drivers of hospital healthcare services; however, high workloads and emotional pressures place them at risk for occupational stress. Transformational leadership is proposed as a managerial style capable of fostering intrinsic motivation and reducing nurse stress levels. Objective: This study aimed to analyze the relationship between transformational leadership, intrinsic motivation, and occupational stress among hospital nurses, while testing the mediating role of intrinsic motivation. Methods: A quantitative study with a cross-sectional design was conducted among 107 active nurses selected through purposive sampling. Data collection instruments included the Global Transformational Leadership Scale (GTL), an Intrinsic Motivation scale based on Self-Determination Theory (SDT), and an Occupational Stress scale based on the Job Demand-Control model. Data analysis comprised descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and mediation analysis via the Baron & Kenny approach, Sobel test, and bootstrapping. Results: Most nurses perceived transformational leadership (4.08 ± 0.52) and intrinsic motivation (4.13 ± 0.36) at high levels, with occupational stress at a moderate level (2.93 ± 0.39). Transformational leadership positively correlated with intrinsic motivation (r = 0.642, p < 0.001) and negatively correlated with job stress (r = -0.323, p < 0.001). Mediation analysis revealed that intrinsic motivation fully mediated the relationship between transformational leadership and job stress (Sobel Z = -2.816, p = 0.0049; 68.9% indirect effect). Conclusion: Transformational leadership reduces nurse job stress indirectly by strengthening intrinsic motivation. Hospital nurse managers should adopt leadership practices focused on supporting autonomy, competence, and relatedness to foster sustainable healthcare environments.

Abstract Tandem mass spectrometry (MS2) is central to small-molecule structural annotation in metabolomics, yet accurate structure inference remains challenging because of complex fragmentation and structurally similar candidates. Here, we introduce MS2Agent, an end-to-end multi-agent framework that integrates cross-modal representation learning with large language model (LLM) reasoning for MS2 annotation. The agent converts mass spectrometry data and molecular structures into a unified textual representation and utilizes a pre-trained model to calculate similarity. Four functional agents perform spectrum textualization, structure textualization, candidate initialization, and collaborative reranking, enabling evidence-based candidate discrimination. On the CASMI 2022 benchmark, MS2Agent improved Recall@1 from 0.156 for the Codex baseline to 0.738 with the same base LLM. Evaluations on MassSpecGym and an independently constructed isomer benchmark further characterize its generalization and performance in challenging structural cases. To improve computational efficiency, we developed MS2Rep-0.8B-GRPO, a lightweight 0.8B-parameter model optimized by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), a reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm for MS2 and molecular-structure textualization, achieving a Recall@1 of 0.784 (+8.4 percentage points over the base model) on the CASMI 2022 benchmark. Tests on real samples further demonstrate the practical utility of MS2Agent for metabolite annotation. This multi-agent framework integrating cross-modal representation learning and LLM reasoning offers a promising strategy for automated structural annotation workflows. Future advances in LLMs may further strengthen the annotation capability of the proposed framework.

Abstract Deep learning (DL) has rapidly advanced automated analysis of retinal fundus images, enabling scalable screening and grading of multiple sight-threatening conditions. This review synthesizes evidence on DL methods for diabetic retinopathy (DR), glaucoma, diabetic macular edema (DME), retinal vessel tortuosity, age-related macular degeneration (ARMD/AMD), macular fibrosis, and fundus neoplasms. We examine preprocessing pipelines, model architectures (CNNs, transformers, hybrids), datasets, evaluation metrics, and clinical performance, drawing on recent systematic reviews, multi-disease benchmarks, and regulator-approved system audits. Findings indicate high accuracy for DR and AMD classification (often >0.90 AUROC/sensitivity), promising but more variable results for glaucoma and DME from fundus alone, and emerging capability for tortuosity quantification and tumor triage. Key challenges include domain shift, data quality/gradability, class imbalance for rare entities (fibrosis, neoplasms), and the need for explainability and external validation. We conclude with recommendations for robust, clinically deployable pipelines and future research directions in multimodal integration and foundation models.

Restaurants are required to respond to menu inquiries, take orders, clarify any customizations, and provide customers with information about the status of their orders all while overseeing the preparation of food and the delivery of in-person service. In times of high demand, the need for multiple customer interactions can overwhelm the staff, lead to longer waiting times, and result in errors when order details are transferred manually. Although digital menus and mobile ordering systems standardise the ordering process, they can force customers to go through fixed menus and forms. This paper outlines the design of a Multilingual Conversational AI for Restaurant Automation system that incorporates both voice and text interaction, multilingual natural language processing (NLP), response generation based on a large language model (LLM), and structured order summarisation. The system takes customer requests via an application or a messaging-oriented interface, converts speech into text where necessary, detects the language and the intent, extracts the food items and the quantities, and uses the restaurant's menu data to produce appropriate contextual responses. A query-summary component converts the conversation into structured order data, containing the names of the items, the quantities, the prices, and the billing information. The architecture is based on a client–server model, with the user interface dealing with the interactions and the backend services handling the AI processing and database operations. The implementation context includes the use of Flutter/Dart, Firebase Authentication, Firebase Firestore, Google Gemini AI, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and an NLP REST API. The paper covers the motivation, related work, architecture, workflow, the various implementation modules, and an evaluation plan. Since the project materials provided do not include controlled benchmark measurements, no claims are made regarding unsupported accuracy, latency, or cost reduction figures.

Clinical internships are a critical stage in the professional socialisation of nursing students, but negative experiences during these internships may lead to a decline in professional identity or even the loss of talent. The Douyin (the Chinese version of TikTok) platform features many internship narratives spontaneously shared by nursing interns, providing a unique data source for understanding their narrative expressions; however, systematic qualitative research on this topic remains lacking. This study explores the thematic characteristics of professional socialisation among nursing interns on the Douyin platform and compares manual thematic analysis with analysis using the DeepSeek R1 large language model in theme identification. Using a human-machine parallel qualitative research design, we collected 40 short videos posted by nursing interns and 431 valid comments from Douyin. We conducted manual thematic analysis (using NVivo 12) and an independent analysis using the DeepSeek R1 large language model. Using Duchscher’s three-stage model of transitional shock as the theoretical framework, we systematically compared the thematic identification results of the two methods. The integrated thematic matrix shows that nursing interns’ narratives revolve around three themes tied to the stages of their clinical practice: the early stage is marked by value conflicts; the middle stage by superficial role identification; and the late stage by a tendency toward either professional self-integration or professional disengagement. This study tentatively summarises the above phenomena as “structural value disconnection,” “the tension between superficial adaptation and deep internalisation,” and “value-integration outcomes” versus “value-disengagement outcomes.” These concepts are inductive descriptions based on cross-sectional data and require further validation through longitudinal research. The three stages correspond to the “Doing-Being-Knowing” framework in Duchscher’s theory of transitional shock and involve three aspects of professional socialisation: acquiring knowledge and skills, internalising values and norms, and forming role identity. Under the specific input conditions of this study (manual exposure to multimodal information, with DeepSeek R1 receiving only text), the two methods showed strong consistency in identifying core themes. At the same time, each captured complementary themes that the other missed. Nursing interns’ narratives reflect thematic patterns tied to the internship phase, showing a progression from value conflicts and superficial adaptation to internalisation or withdrawal. The complementary nature of manual analysis and large language model analysis provides a methodological framework for qualitative research in nursing. The findings suggest that educators should integrate value guidance throughout the entire clinical practicum process and, through measures such as pre-practicum psychological preparation, improvement of the mentor-student relationship, and comprehensive psychological support mechanisms, facilitate students’ transition from behavioural compliance to value alignment.

Introduction: Traditional pharmaceutical development faces critical challenges: drug development costs exceed $2.6 billion per approved drug, timelines extend 10-15 years, and 40% of new chemical entities demonstrate inadequate bioavailability. Conventional approaches rely on empirical screening generating 50-100 kg waste per kilogram of active pharmaceutical ingredient. The pharmaceutical industry urgently requires transformative innovation integrating computational intelligence, advanced delivery systems, and sustainable manufacturing. Methods: This comprehensive review integrates three complementary technological paradigms: (1) QSAR-powered artificial intelligence employing machine learning algorithms for computational drug discovery, reducing chemical synthesis requirements by 85-90%; (2) Nanotechnology-enabled delivery systems (liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, cubosomes, transethosomes) overcoming biological barriers and enhancing bioavailability 10-100 fold; and (3) Green chemistry principles enabling sustainable synthesis through catalytic reactions, biocatalysis, and continuous manufacturing, reducing waste generation by 60-90%. Results: Integrated QSAR-nano-green chemistry approaches demonstrate remarkable benefits compared to conventional methods: 92% waste reduction (95 kg → 8 kg per kilogram product), 82% energy reduction (250 → 45 kWh/kg), 47% cost reduction ($650 → $343/kg), and 92% timeline acceleration (48 → 4 hours). QSAR screening reduces experimental compounds from 200-300 to 15-20, while nanoformulations enhance bioavailability and targeting efficiency. Green chemistry manufacturing achieves pharmaceutical-grade quality with minimal environmental burden. Conclusion: Synergistic convergence of QSAR, nanotechnology, and green chemistry represents paradigm shift in pharmaceutical innovation. This integrated approach enables development of therapeutics that are more effective, safer, more sustainable, and economically accessible globally democratizing drug development across academic, industry, and developing country sectors.

Long-running agent workflows can lose task scope, source custody, authority, current environment state, unresolved conflicts, or knowledge of what another worker is doing. Operational Epistemic Situational Awareness (ESA) is proposed as the capability to maintain and query an evidence-qualified model of those conditions and to govern continuation when that model becomes stale, conflicted, missing, or outside authority. The architecture uses a governed meaning substrate as an orchestration sidecar, but a sidecar is not awareness by itself. Agent check-ins can be false or stale; receipts can record claims without proving effects; exclusive task claims can deadlock; handoffs can be unaccepted; and unmediated tools can bypass the substrate. The system must distinguish asserted, observed, inferred, stale, conflicted, and unknown state; combine voluntary reports with independent observations; preserve liveness and recovery; and govern sensitive operational data. This paper defines an operational state model, check-in and claim leases, accepted handoff capsules, evidence postures, refusal and escalation outcomes, bypass and availability conditions, cold-boot orientation through the Governed Meaning Base, realization funnel, and comparative evaluation. It makes no claim of consciousness or privileged agent self-knowledge.

BACKGROUND: Multimorbidity and functional decline become increasingly prevalent with age, particularly in those near the end of life. This poses critical challenges for both families and society in providing adequate care. However, it remains unclear which type of care yields better outcomes. AIM: To systematically assess the impact of informal care, formal care, and a combination of both on health outcomes, healthcare utilization, and costs of care for older adults near the end of life. DESIGN: A systematic review with narrative synthesis was registered on PROSPERO (CRD42024512003). Screening was assisted by machine learning tool ASReview, and study quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, with support from large language model TXYZ.AI. DATA SOURCES: Articles published between database inception and June 4th, 2025 were identified in PubMed, Embase, and CINAHL. RESULTS: Thirty-six studies, including 20 observational and 16 interventional were included. Most observational studies examined place of death, with some associations involving informal care pointing towards lower home death or greater hospital death. In contrast, physician and nurse home visits were associated with a greater likelihood of home death. Specialized formal care interventions generally reported improvements in quality of life and reductions in healthcare use. Quality assessment showed 85.2% AI-human agreement, with 44.4% of studies meeting all seven quality criteria. DISCUSSION: Informal care did not necessarily facilitate home death, whereas formal home-based care was linked to a greater likelihood of home death. Interventional evidence also suggests broader benefits of specialized formal care, although certainty was limited by methodological concerns.

Background: Healthcare facilities with limited resources face various challenges in early detection and emergency referral systems, including shortages of healthcare personnel, inadequate infrastructure, and the limited accuracy of conventional screening methods. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has the potential to serve as a solution to improve the quality of clinical decision-making under these conditions. Objective: This scientific paper aims to identify and synthesize current evidence regarding the use of AI in early detection, early warning systems, and triage. Methods: This study is a narrative review using the PubMed and Google Scholar databases. English-language articles published between 2019 and 2026 that discussed the implementation of AI in early detection or emergency referral systems in resource-limited settings were included. Of the 2,376 articles identified, 16 met the inclusion criteria. Results: The articles were predominantly focused on early detection and early warning systems (50%), followed by triage and referral systems (31%), and health system strengthening (19%). Machine Learning and Deep Learning were the most commonly used AI methods. Several studies demonstrated high performance, with AUC values ranging from 0.80 to 0.97. AI was shown to improve the accuracy of sepsis detection, patient prioritization, and support faster and more objective referral decision-making. Conclusion: AI has the potential to enhance early detection, triage, and emergency referral systems in healthcare facilities with limited resources, although its implementation continues to face challenges related to infrastructure, user trust, as well as regulatory and data governance aspects.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Abstrak Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk mengkaji pemanfaatan Artificial Intelligence (AI) secara teologis sebagai sarana pendukung penginjilan digital bagi Generasi Z melalui media sosial. Perkembangan AI dan media sosial telah mengubah cara Generasi Z berkomunikasi, memperoleh informasi, membangun relasi, dan berinteraksi dengan pesan-pesan keagamaan. Perubahan tersebut memberikan peluang baru bagi gereja untuk memberitakan Injil melalui berbagai platform digital, sekaligus menghadirkan tantangan teologis dan etis berkaitan dengan autentisitas, tanggung jawab manusia, otoritas Kitab Suci, pengaruh algoritma, dan dimensi relasional dalam penginjilan. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kualitatif deskriptif melalui studi kepustakaan terhadap berbagai kajian teologis, misiologis, dan interdisipliner mengenai AI, teologi digital, media sosial, Generasi Z, dan penginjilan Kristen. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa AI dapat mendukung penginjilan digital melalui produksi konten, penerjemahan, personalisasi pesan, pengembangan visual, dan perluasan jangkauan pemberitaan Injil. Namun, AI tidak dapat menggantikan manusia sebagai saksi Kristus karena tidak memiliki iman, pengalaman spiritual, tanggung jawab moral, dan kehadiran relasional sebagaimana manusia. Oleh karena itu, AI perlu ditempatkan sebagai sarana misi, bukan subjek misi. Kristus tetap menjadi pusat Injil, Kitab Suci menjadi dasar pemberitaan, manusia menjadi saksi, AI berfungsi sebagai sarana pendukung, media sosial menjadi ruang komunikasi dan perjumpaan, sedangkan arah akhir penginjilan digital adalah terbentuknya relasi dan pemuridan. Kata-kata kunci: Artificial Intelligence, penginjilan digital, Generasi Z, media sosial, teologi digital, pemuridan abstract The purpose of this study is to examine the theological use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a supporting medium for digital evangelism among Generation Z through social media. The rapid development of AI and social media has transformed the way Generation Z communicates, obtains information, builds relationships, and encounters religious messages. This transformation provides new opportunities for the church to proclaim the gospel through digital platforms, while also raising theological and ethical challenges concerning authenticity, human responsibility, biblical authority, algorithmic influence, and the relational nature of evangelism. This study employs a descriptive qualitative method through a literature review of theological, missiological, and interdisciplinary studies concerning AI, digital theology, social media, Generation Z, and Christian evangelism. The findings indicate that AI can support digital evangelism through content production, translation, personalization, visual development, and wider dissemination of gospel messages. However, AI cannot replace human beings as witnesses of Christ because it does not possess faith, spiritual experience, moral responsibility, or relational presence. Therefore, AI should be positioned as a means of mission rather than a subject of mission. Christ remains the center of the gospel, Scripture remains the foundation of its message, human beings remain witnesses, AI functions as a supporting tool, social media becomes a space for communication and encounter, and the ultimate direction of digital evangelism is relationship and discipleship. Key words: Artificial Intelligence, digital evangelism, Z Generation, social media, digital theology, discipleship

The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (Generative AI), such as ChatGPT, has brought significant changes to higher education, including Arabic language learning for non-native speakers (Arabic as a Foreign Language). Writing skills (Maharah al-Kitabah) are considered a relatively complex productive skill. Learners are required not only to master word formation (Sarf) and Arabic grammar (Nahwu), but also to organize ideas coherently and logically. This article employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach based on the PRISMA 2020 standards to map the use of ChatGPT in Arabic writing, examine the reliability of AI in Arabic grammar, and identify research gaps that remain underexplored. The review findings indicate that ChatGPT can serve as a useful writing partner (human-AI co-writer), particularly for generating ideas, enriching vocabulary, and correcting basic grammatical errors. However, AI still frequently produces errors or “hallucinations” when dealing with morphologically complex words, variations in Arabic dialects, and unvocalized texts. As a result, AI-generated writing may appear linguistically polished on the surface while containing grammatical inaccuracies. Furthermore, excessive reliance on AI may pose risks to academic integrity, while AI detection tools themselves often produce inaccurate results when identifying Arabic-language texts (false positives). This review also finds that existing research remains overly focused on English, tends to examine only the final writing outcomes without investigating students’ cognitive processes, and has paid limited attention to AI models specifically developed for the Arab region, such as ALLaM and Jais. Therefore, the approach to AI-assisted learning needs to shift from merely using AI toward purposeful and reflective utilization through frameworks such as the Spiral Learning Model and Genre-Based Pedagogy, so that AI functions as a scaffold without diminishing students’ autonomy and critical thinking.

Perkembangan e-commerce mendorong platform digital untuk menghadirkan berbagai strategi pemasaran guna meningkatkan keputusan pembelian konsumen. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Live Shopping, Promosi Berbasis Artificial Intelligence (AI), dan Perceived Trust terhadap keputusan pembelian pengguna e-commerce Lazada. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan pengumpulan data melalui kuesioner kepada pengguna Lazada. Data dianalisis menggunakan regresi linier berganda dan pengujian hipotesis secara parsial. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Live Shopping tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian, dengan nilai signifikansi 0,223. Sebaliknya, Promosi Berbasis AI berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian dengan nilai signifikansi 0,005. Perceived Trust juga terbukti berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian dengan nilai signifikansi 0,002. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa konsumen Lazada lebih terdorong oleh promosi yang relevan dan personal serta rasa percaya terhadap platform dibandingkan pengalaman berbelanja melalui siaran langsung. Penelitian ini memberikan gambaran bahwa pemanfaatan AI dan peningkatan kepercayaan konsumen dapat menjadi strategi penting dalam mendorong keputusan pembelian pada e-commerce.

Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang meja belajar lipat minimalis yang ergonomis dan berorientasi pada pengguna di lingkungan perguruan tinggi, menjawab tantangan keterbatasan ruang hunian mahasiswa. Penelitian perancangan produk ini melibatkan 30 responden mahasiswa dengan karakteristik usia rata-rata 21 hingga 23 tahun, jenis kelamin pria dan wanita, tinggi badan rata-rata 160 cm, di fakultas teknik yang dipilih secara purposive sampling. Metode yang digunakan meliputi Ergonomic Function Deployment (EFD) untuk menerjemahkan kebutuhan pengguna menjadi karakteristik teknis, pengukuran antropometri untuk validasi dimensi fisik, dan Morphology Product untuk pengembangan alternatif desain yang mengintegrasikan kearifan lokal. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan penerjemahan delapan kebutuhan pengguna menjadi target teknis presisi, seperti tinggi meja 72 cm dan dimensi lipat 60 cm. Data antropometri selanjutnya memvalidasi dimensi tersebut secara objektif, memastikan kesesuaian postur dan ruang kaki yang inklusif bagi berbagai tipe tubuh. Tahap morfologi menghasilkan konfigurasi optimal berupa meja bersudut membulat, mekanisme flat folding yang aman, rangka aluminium hollow, serta sentuhan finishing natural beraksen lokal betawi. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa integrasi EFD, antropometri, dan morfologi produk sangat efektif menghasilkan furnitur edukatif yang tidak hanya memecahkan masalah efisiensi ruang dan kenyamanan postur, tetapi juga memiliki nilai kultural. Luaran penelitian ini menghasilkan rancangan teknis dan prototype konseptual (model CAD) dan analisis kelayakan manufaktur yang belum dilakukan pada tahap ini. Penelitian ini berkontribusi pada integrasi EFD, antropometri, dan morfologi produk dalam perancangan furnitur edukatif yang hemat ruang, ergonomis, dan bernilai kultural.

This systematic review assessed the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI) for detecting periapical periodontitis on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). A systematic literature search of Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase was conducted to identify peer-reviewed diagnostic studies involving human participants and published up to August 30, 2026. Studies evaluating the application of AI for the detection of periapical periodontitis on CBCT were deemed eligible for inclusion. Conversely, studies focusing exclusively on periapical cysts, other odontogenic lesions, or root resorption were excluded. The risk of bias was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies–Artificial Intelligence (QUADAS-AI) tool, while the certainty of the evidence for the pooled outcomes was evaluated according to the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Of 659 records identified through database searches, 18 studies were included in the systematic review and 6 in the meta-analysis. The exploratory HSROC synthesis yielded a pooled sensitivity of 0.91 (95% CI, 0.84-0.94) and a pooled specificity of 0.94 (95% CI, 0.80-0.98). Substantial between-study heterogeneity was observed, with I² values exceeding 98% for virtually all reported metrics, and the corresponding prediction regions were wide. Consequently, the pooled estimates should be interpreted solely as exploratory descriptive summaries rather than as clinically generalisable estimates of diagnostic performance. The GRADE certainty of evidence was rated as very low for each of the four pooled outcomes. The diagnostic performance and clinical utility of AI for the detection of periapical periodontitis on CBCT remain uncertain, owing to the extreme heterogeneity, wide prediction regions, and very low certainty of evidence identified in this review. These findings support further investigation rather than routine clinical implementation at present. AI warrants further evaluation as a potential adjunct to clinician-led assessment of periapical periodontitis. The current evidence does not establish clinical benefit or justify recommending routine use or replacement of professional judgement.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Abstract Thermal energy storage (TES) using phase change material (PCM) is one of the key technologies to improve energy efficiency and integrate renewable energy. This study aims to systematically map the research evolution, emerging themes, major contributors, and technological developments in PCM-based TES research from 2000 to 2025. A PRISMA-based bibliometric analysis was conducted using 5612 publications retrieved from the Scopus database and analyzed using Bibliometrix and VOSviewer. The analysis examines publication trends, leading countries and journals, collaboration networks, citation patterns, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic evolution. With an above 60% share of the publications after 2018, it shows the rapid development in this field, with China and India being the main contributors. The research areas have developed from the fundamental characterization of PCMs to nano- and composite PCMs, heat transfer enhancement, battery thermal management, building energy applications, and sustainable energy systems. The application of artificial intelligence and machine learning in TES modeling, prediction, optimization, and intelligent control is shown in emerging research clusters, which demonstrates a growing trend. The findings identify key research directions and gaps, particularly in optimizing nano/composite PCM formulations, validating PCM performance under realistic operating conditions, and developing experimentally validated AI/ML models. This review offers a structured knowledge of the development of PCM-based TES research and identifies some specific opportunities for the development of efficient, reliable, and application-oriented thermal energy storage technologies.

Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has developed from a specialised area of computer science into a general-purpose technology that increasingly influences education, healthcare, finance, employment, communication, governance and everyday decision-making. This expansion makes AI not only a technological subject but also a philosophical and ethical concern. This conceptual research paper examines the relationship between philosophy, ethics and artificial intelligence from a human-centred perspective. It analyses the ethical significance of human dignity, autonomy, privacy, justice, fairness, transparency, accountability, responsibility and sustainability. The study uses qualitative conceptual analysis of philosophical literature, AI ethics scholarship and major institutional frameworks. Particular attention is given to deontological ethics, consequentialism, virtue ethics and selected Indian ethical ideas. The paper further examines algorithmic bias, surveillance, opacity, manipulation, employment transformation, education, environmental impact and the problem of assigning responsibility for AI-mediated decisions. Contemporary frameworks of UNESCO, OECD, NIST and NITI Aayog are examined as important attempts to translate ethical principles into governance and risk-management practices. The analysis indicates that responsible AI cannot be achieved by technical safeguards alone. Ethical reasoning needs to be integrated across the complete AI lifecycle, from problem formulation and data selection to design, testing, deployment, monitoring and retirement. A human-centred framework is proposed around eight principles: human dignity, human agency, non-maleficence, justice and inclusion, privacy, explainability and contestability, accountability, and sustainability. The paper concludes that the fundamental question for the AI era is not merely what machines can do, but what human purposes, values and limits should guide their development and use.

documents.abstract: This book examines the transformation of labour in the emerging platform economy, focusing on gig workers, employment insecurity, and social protection. It explores how digital platforms are reshaping employment relationships, working conditions, income stability, and labour rights. The book highlights key challenges such as algorithmic management, lack of social security, and economic vulnerability. It also discusses labour policies, legal frameworks, and social protection measures to promote fair employment, workers' welfare, and inclusive economic development.

Abstract Precision agriculture amalgamates artificial intelligence (AI) with field-level sensors to enhance agricultural yield while reducing resource use. This article offers an extensive examination of the application of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) methodologies to two essential functions: forecasting crop production based on environmental and soil information, and identifying plant diseases using leaf images. We investigate the historical evolution of the discipline, outline prevalent data sources and preprocessing methodologies, evaluate the reported efficacy of prominent model families across various benchmark analyses, showcase representative case-study workflows, and assess the resource and economic implications of AI-assisted agriculture. We provide a deeper examination of regional deployment trends, delineate the practical and technological obstacles hindering large-scale implementation, and suggest prospective research avenues such as federated learning, edge deployment, and interpretable AI. The evaluation aims to function as a comprehensive resource for scholars and professionals exploring this swiftly advancing domain.

Given the complexity of personality, we might assume that significant behaviour is required to express our traits. Here we use large language models (LLMs) to test the extent to which personality is visible in short conversations with artificial intelligence (AI). In a preregistered experiment, 100 participants completed the Big-Five Inventory (BFI) before having unstructured conversations with GPT-4.1, writing a median of 430 words. We then instructed a second LLM rater (Claude Sonnet 4.6) to complete the BFI for each participant, predicting their responses based solely on an analysis of the participant-GPT chats. Correlations between LLM-predicted and self-reported BFI traits were significant (range r = .25 to .47), in some cases matching previously documented self-other predictions from family members. A linguistic analysis revealed that the LLM rater’s predictions relied largely on lexical content as opposed to syntax. Using preexisting data, we tested if the AI’s persona influenced how much participants revealed about themselves in conversation. A hundred participants chatted with two versions of GPT-4.1—one that mirrored their personality (mirror AI) and one that opposed it (inverse AI). The LLM rater predicted BFI traits based on the interactions and we correlated this prediction with self-report. Mirror chats generated significant correlations, averaging r = .41; for inverse chats the average fell to r = .30, dropping to zero when the prediction relied on lexical content alone. People readily convey their personality profile in short conversations with AI, and this is enhanced when the AI’s persona mirrors the users.

Although English is taught in Afghan universities, the factors that motivate students in Helmand Province to learn it remain under-researched. This study examined how intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and English learning confidence shape overall motivation to learn English in Helmand Province, Afghanistan. A quantitative correlational design was used to collect data through a structured questionnaire from 324 male students across four universities (Helmand University, Bost University, Arakozia University, and Wadie Helmand University) using multi-stage stratified random sampling. Each construct was measured using five items rated on a 5-point Likert scale. The study used descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Pearson correlation, paired-sample t-test, and multiple regression. The results indicated high overall motivational levels (M = 4.39, SD = 0.63), and intrinsic motivation (M = 4.38, SD = 0.53) was significantly higher than extrinsic motivation (M = 3.95, SD = 0.83), t = 10.03, p <. 001. The correlational analysis revealed a significant positive correlation among all variables (p < .001), and English learning confidence had the strongest correlation with overall motivation (r = .623). The multiple regression analysis indicated that the three predictors explained 45.4% of the variance in overall motivation (R2 =.454). The findings suggest that while both intrinsic and extrinsic motivations are important, students in the target universities are highly influenced by internal factors. This study emphasizes the importance of psychological factors in sustaining motivation among university students in Helmand Province.

Low back pain (LBP) remains one of the most common occupational health problems among nursing professions worldwide, particularly in high-demand units such as the intensive care unit (ICU), where high physical workload and psychological stress coexist. Recognising its multifactorial origins is essential for effective preventive strategies. The objective of this study is to determine the prevalence of LBP and identify associated risk factors among ICU nurses at Ampang hospital Malaysia. A cross-sectional study was conducted among ICU nurses. Validated questionnaires were used to collect demographics data, prevalence and occupational risk factors of LBP. Descriptive statistics were applied, chi-square tests assessed associations between sex and pain-related variables, and multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of LBP. Fifty ICU nurses participated (94% female; predominantly aged 31–40 years). The prevalence of moderate-to-severe LBP was high, with significant sex differences in pain intensity (p = 0.012). Body Mass Index (BMI) emerged as a major individual risk factor (OR 3.64, p = 0.018). Among workplace variables, daily working hours were the only significant predictor (OR 0.9, p = 0.009), indicating an incremental rise in LBP risk with longer shifts. Other factors were not statistically significant. The findings confirm that LBP is highly prevalent among ICU nurses and is strongly associated with modifiable individual and organisational factors. Excess body weight and prolonged working hours likely exacerbate biomechanical strain and cumulative lumbar load in intensive care settings. Keywords Low back pain, intensive care, nurses, occupational health, ergonomics
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) structures rely on large amounts of private records for training and deployment. This creates privacy concerns that common fact safety systems now would not have been designed to handle, along with opaque statistical series, net scraping without meaningful consent, inferences about sensitive features, leakage of training statistics from models, surveillance, and automated decision making. The rapid development of generative AI has heightened those concerns, as fashions that are proficient on internet-scale data currently are used by tens of millions of those who mechanically embed private records into them. It assesses the main legal frameworks, particularly the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the EU AI Act, and India’s Digital Personal Information Protection Act, 2023, and identifies gaps in how they handle inferred facts, educated fashions, and enforcement of erasure rights. It also considers regulatory enforcement enjoy, consisting of actions against Clearview AI and ChatGPT, to show how current regulation is applied to AI in practice. Finally, it evaluates technical security measures consisting of differential privacy and connected knowing, along with organizational measures consisting of privacy-by-design, impact assessments, and independent audits. The paper argues that effective security requires the implementation of legal responsibilities mixed with privacy-preserving engineering, instead of either on my own, and that responsibility should be shifted upstream to people who design, train, and deploy AI systems. It concludes with suggestions for regulators, with special reference to the Indian context.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Generation Alpha (born 2010-2024) and Generation Beta (born 2025-2039) represent an unprecedented developmental archetype defined by total digital integration and ubiquitous artificial intelligence (AI). This empirical study evaluated specialized psychological adaptation mechanisms, parenting models, and mental health intervention frameworks across these cohorts. Utilizing a mixed-methods design, quantitative data were gathered from $N = 300$ parents (Gen Alpha parents and expectant/early Gen Beta parents) using the Modified Parental Stress Scale (PSS) and Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL), supplemented by qualitative interviews with $N = 20$ pediatric mental health experts. Independent samples $t$-tests confirmed that Gen Alpha/Beta display significantly higher digital dependency anxiety ($M = 38.60, p < .001$) alongside superior visual-spatial intelligence ($M = 44.10, p < .001$) relative to normative baselines. Crucially, a proactive "Digital Integration" co-navigation parenting framework yielded significantly lower parental stress ($M = 29.50$) compared to rigid "Digital Detox" restriction models ($M = 42.80, p < .001$). A preventive clinical framework focusing on Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) and cognitive impulse management is proposed.
topics: Child and Adolescent Psychosocial and Emotional Development

documents.abstract: A psychologically friendly school environment is related to school well-being and student involvement in learning. Although these two aspects have been extensively researched, empirical evidence in the context of Islamic primary schools in Indonesia still needs to be expanded. This study aims to describe school welfare and student involvement and analyze the relationship between the two in grades IV–VI. The study uses a quantitative approach with an ex post facto correlational design. A total of 57 students were selected through purposive sampling techniques. Data were collected using a Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed through descriptive statistics, normality tests, linearity tests, and simple linear regression. The results showed that school well-being and student involvement were in the moderate category. There was a positive and significant relationship between the two variables (Y = 7.756 + 0.484X; t = 4.744; p < 0.001; R = 0.539). A value of R² = 0.290 indicates that school well-being explains 29% of the variation in student engagement. These findings enrich the empirical evidence in the context of Islamic primary education and emphasize the importance of strengthening positive relationships between students and designing learning that encourages cognitive engagement. The cross-sectional design does not allow for the drawing of cause-and-effect conclusions.

Abstract Digital technology has become an important component of contemporary public-health systems. Telemedicine, mobile health applications, electronic health records, digital identity, health information systems, remote monitoring, artificial intelligence and data analytics can support prevention, early detection, referral, continuity of care and population-level surveillance. India has developed a substantial digital-health ecosystem, including the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) and eSanjeevani. WHO describes digital health as an area with major potential to improve access, decision-making and health-system performance, while also emphasizing equity, interoperability and responsible implementation. [1–5] This paper examines the relationship between public health and digital technology with special reference to Parbhani district of Maharashtra. It uses a narrative review and policy-analysis approach based on WHO documents, Government of India sources, Census material and recent peer-reviewed literature. The paper discusses potential applications in primary healthcare, maternal and child health, nutrition, noncommunicable disease management, infectious-disease surveillance, health education and referral services. Particular attention is given to the rural–urban digital divide, digital literacy, connectivity, privacy, cybersecurity, interoperability and workforce readiness. A district-level framework is proposed to connect community-level workers with digital registration, teleconsultation, electronic records and public-health analytics. The paper argues that technology should complement rather than replace human-centred public-health services. For Parbhani, a phased approach combining infrastructure, training, assisted digital access, data governance and local evaluation can support more equitable digital health development.

With the extended SEQUAL framework presented in Chap 3 , we can examine aspects of the quality of models for man and machines more systematically. We start with an example of how to assess the quality of symbolic models for human use, building on earlier work using SEQUAL to evaluate ontologies, and extending it to include aspects of the renewed framework. Then we present a case study of a machine learning system in which the quality of the results depends on both symbolic and sub-symbolic models. In Sect. 4.3, we discuss how sustainability considerations are important when selecting ML techniques for data at various points along the pipeline. Section 4.4 ends the chapter by investigating the quality of explanation models in XAI.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: This paper investigates the intersections of race, corporate professionalism, and somatic regulation within Brazilian Sign Language (Libras) translation and interpretation. While traditional translation scholarship prioritizes linguistic neutrality, this study employs an interdisciplinary critical methodology combining Critical Race Theory (CRT), Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA), and Translation and Interpreting Studies (TIS) to deconstruct how standard professional aesthetics inadvertently sustain systemic racism and Eurocentric cultural erasure. Utilizing a textual deconstruction of Article 5 of the National Libras Code of Ethics alongside an autoethnographic mapping of workplace visual ergonomics, we examine how racialized aesthetic expectations regulate and pathologize cultural markers such as braided hairstyles, Black power aesthetics, and turbans. Furthermore, we analyze technical workplace barriers through a TIS lens, including contrastive shirt mandates, stage lighting calibration, and professional turn-taking ergonomics. By interrogating these parameters, we expose the underlying institutional discourses and translational norms that pressure Black interpreters to alter their unalterable phenotypes to comply with a normalized, white somatic standard, ultimately arguing for an anti-racist reconfiguration of interpreter ethics and material practices.

Background: Radiotherapy is a complex process involving many professions and many handovers of information, with error opportunities at every step. Most errors are intercepted before they reach the patient, and radiation therapists (RTTs), who carry out the final verification and delivery steps, are the professional group that most often detects them. Objective: To review the evidence on how RTTs detect, report and learn from near-miss events, and to propose a framework for strengthening this human safety barrier. Methods: A narrative mini-review of peer-reviewed literature, incident learning system reports (ROSIS, SAFRON, RO-ILS), professional guidance (AAPM, ASTRO, ICRP, IAEA, WHO, UK safer-radiotherapy publications) and human-factors research. Results: Errors arise most often in planning, simulation and documentation, but therapists are the largest single group of discoverers in multi-institutional and international databases. RTTs detect errors through independent verification, image-guided review (CBCT, kV/MV, surface guidance), observation in the treatment room and communication with the team. Detection is shaped by training, workload, situation awareness and the design of technology. Reporting is limited by fear of reprimand, hierarchy, slow systems and cognitive biases that make intercepted events seem not worth reporting. Psychological safety and just-culture principles increase reporting. Learning requires analysis at the level of the system, corrective action and feedback. Automation reduces some errors but creates new failure modes and automation bias. Conclusions: RTTs are active safety barriers, not passive operators. We propose a Detect-Intercept-Report-Analyze-Learn-Improve-Reassess framework with RTT competencies defined for each stage, and we call for standard definitions, RTT-led investigation, safety competencies in RTT education, and AI that supports rather than replaces the vigilance of RTTs.

Annotatsiya: Mazkur maqolada zamonaviy qurilish loyihalarini boshqarishda Building Information Modeling (BIM) texnologiyasidan foydalanishning ilmiy va amaliy jihatlari tadqiq etilgan. BIM texnologiyasining 3D modellashtirishdan tashqari loyiha ma’lumotlarini boshqarish, qurilish jarayonlarini muvofiqlashtirish, vaqt va xarajatlarni nazorat qilish hamda obyektning ekspluatatsiya bosqichidagi ma’lumotlarni boshqarish imkoniyatlari tahlil qilingan. BIM texnologiyasining Common Data Environment (CDE), openBIM, IFC, 4D va 5D modellashtirish, Internet of Things (IoT), sun’iy intellekt va Digital Twin texnologiyalari bilan integratsiyasi ko‘rib chiqilgan. Tadqiqot natijasida BIM asosida qurilish loyihalarini boshqarishning integratsiyalashgan modeli taklif etilgan. Shuningdek, O‘zbekiston qurilish sohasida BIM texnologiyalarini joriy etishning mavjud holati va rivojlanish istiqbollari tahlil qilinib, BIM mutaxassislarini tayyorlash, elektron hujjat aylanishi va raqamli axborot muhitini rivojlantirish bo‘yicha takliflar ishlab chiqilgan. Kalit so‘zlar: BIM, raqamli qurilish, raqamli transformatsiya, 3D modellashtirish, 4D BIM, 5D BIM, CDE, openBIM, IFC, Digital Twin, IoT, sun’iy intellekt, qurilish boshqaruvi. Abstract: This article examines the scientific and practical aspects of using Building Information Modeling (BIM) technology for managing modern construction projects. The study analyzes BIM not only as a three-dimensional modeling technology but also as an integrated information management approach for coordinating project participants, controlling construction time and costs, and managing information throughout the life cycle of a building. The integration of BIM with Common Data Environment (CDE), openBIM, IFC, 4D and 5D modeling, Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence, and Digital Twin technologies is considered. Based on the analysis, an integrated BIM-based construction project management model is proposed. The current development and implementation of BIM technologies in the construction sector of Uzbekistan are also discussed. Particular attention is paid to BIM education, electronic document management, information exchange, and the development of digital construction management infrastructure. The proposed approach can contribute to improving project coordination, reducing information inconsistencies, increasing resource efficiency, and supporting data-driven decision-making throughout the construction life cycle. Keywords: BIM, digital construction, digital transformation, 3D modeling, 4D BIM, 5D BIM, CDE, openBIM, IFC, Digital Twin, IoT, artificial intelligence, construction management.

The comprehensive and high-value utilization of crop straw biomass (CSB) is pivotal to advancing sustainable agricultural development and achieving the dual-carbon goals, owing to its low-carbon nature, renewability, and abundance. However, the efficient exploitation of CSB is severely hindered by its structural recalcitrance and heterogeneity, making an effective pretreatment technology to overcome this bottleneck. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have been considered as the most promising green solvents for CSB pretreatment, which not only possess excellent properties but also exhibit prominent advantages including low toxicity, low preparation cost, good biodegradability and recyclability. This review elaborates on the latest research progress of the DESs (especially novel supramolecular DESs) in CSB pretreatment. It further summarizes cutting‑edge DES‑coupled pretreatment technologies, machine‑learning‑assisted DES optimization, techno‑economic analysis and life‑cycle assessment for DES‑based biorefinery. Mitigation strategies and future research directions are proposed, including polyol‑assisted suppression of lignin condensation, machine‑learning‑driven DES screening, and multi‑dimensional mechanistic exploration via advanced characterization and theoretical simulations. Moreover, the review summarizes the diverse high-value application pathways of DES-pretreated CSB in the generation of platform chemicals, biofuels and materials. The challenges faced in the scaling-up of DES-based pretreatment technology to industrial applications are analyzed. Frontier research opportunities are also highlighted, encompassing the development of advanced analytical tools, integrated characterization of interactions between lignin and carbohydrates, and artificial intelligence‑driven innovation within biorefinery systems. The review provides a theoretical basis and practical guidance for the development of lignocellulosic biorefinery approaches, and is of great significance for alleviating the global energy crisis and addressing major environmental issues.

Islamic civilization is one of the major civilizations that has significantly contributed to the development of science and education worldwide. During its golden age, it established educational institutions, fostered scholarly traditions, and produced influential scholars whose ideas continue to shape modern knowledge in the digital era. This article examines the relevance of Islamic civilizational values to the development of modern education through qualitative library research using thematic content analysis. The findings show that Islamic education was distinguished by four interrelated values, namely a strong culture of literacy, the integration of religious and general knowledge, an emphasis on moral formation (akhlak), and openness to knowledge from other civilizations, which together enabled scholars to advance science while upholding ethical and social responsibility. These values are highly relevant to addressing contemporary educational challenges, including declining critical literacy, uncritical dependence on digital technology and artificial intelligence, and the ongoing crisis of learners’ character. These values can inform the development of a modern educational system that integrates critical thinking, digital literacy, character education, and lifelong learning while maintaining moral and social responsibility.
keywords: integration of religious and general knowledge

documents.abstract: Abstract Integration of AI in the educational system is rapidly changing the face of education by offering new possibilities of personalized learning and efficient management at the same time creating serious issues related to student autonomy, data security, and psychology. The paper suggests a holistic framework for the management of AI in education by using recommendations for the responsible use of AI in various spheres developed by international organizations like UNESCO together with recent findings about the psychological state of students. We suggest that successful integration of AI into educational practices should be based on a transition from technology-based management of AI to human-based one where student well-being becomes one of the major ethical considerations.
